400329.title: Ko Ryeo-myeong: Podo
400329.overview: Ko Ryeo-myeong photographs the small world of objects too fine for the eye to catch, shooting them close up and printing them large. He still works with an analogue camera and a special film made for astronomical observation, which gives the prints a colour and texture ordinary photography does not have, and his compositions leave generous empty space so the eye settles on the subject. The Podo (grape) series, his best known, treats a single bunch of grapes as a small universe, completed with other materials and digital colouring.

400328.title: Kim Kang-yong: Reality Image
400328.overview: Kim Kang-yong has been known for decades as Korea's 'brick painter', a realist who painted identical mass-produced bricks during the country's rush of industrialisation in the 1970s as a way of looking at the anonymous, overlooked parts of a city. This solo show at Pyo Gallery, running from 2 to 31 October 2026, traces how the work moved on: from the bricks themselves to the gaps between them, to light, shadow, surface and space. He no longer paints bricks at all. What remains are cubes, intervals and shadows, built from real sand and paint so that a flat surface reads as depth.
